               <ns0:head>CHAP. II.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p n="1">1 BUt I determined this with my self, that I would not come again to you in heavi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">One reason why I put off my formerly intended journey to you, was, That I might give you time to repent, and reform those disorders that were amongst you, that my coming to you might neither cause heaviness in you, seeing me come with a rod, to chide and reprove you; nor yet in my self, who <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> not delight in censures and chidings, but must my self have been sad to have seen such errors and disorders amongst you, as I must by my paternal and Apostolical Authority have cor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rected.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 For if I make you sorry, who is he then that maketh me glad, but the same that is made sorry by me? <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">When I am there, I have no refreshment, or joy in that <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> of the Citizens who are Pagans, all my joy is in that part which are Christians, and constitute the Church of God in that C<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>y: So as I could have had no pleasure or joy in my being there, if I had had nothing but occasion of sadness and hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viness from you, in whom was all my expectation of any joy o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> refreshing.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 And I wrote this same unto you, lest when I came, I <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 12.21.</ns0:note> should have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice, <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 8.22 <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 3.10.</ns0:note> having confidence in you all, that my joy is <ns0:hi>the joy</ns0:hi> of you all <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">This hath been the cause of my writing this second Epi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stle to you, before I my self came in person, that you might have a time more fully and perfectly to reform such things as <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> amongst you, and I have formerly given you notice of; lest when I come, i<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>stead of rejoycing in you, as I ought to do, or having any just occasion so to do, I might meet with what would give me nothing but trouble and sadness; which would not only be grievous to me, but would be con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trary to you<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> duty, for I ought to rejoyce in you, and you <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> so <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>o behave your selves, that I may have cause to re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />joyce in you. And I have confidence in the most of you, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> in all you who are sincere, that you would all be glad to <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ee <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e glad and chearful<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> rejoycing in my society with you.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 For out of much affliction and anguish of heart, I wrote unto you with many tears, not that ye should be grieved, but that ye might know the love which I have more abundantly unto you <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Every man that deriveth from God, is in this made par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />taker of the Divine Nature, that like as God doth not grieve willingly, nor willingly afflict the children of men, so neither will he; but if by reason of his office or trust reposed in him, he be under an obligation sometimes to speak smartly, or to chastise and punish others for their Errors, yet he will so do it, as one that hath no pleasure and delight in it. This the good Judge weepeth, or at least sheweth sorrow and compas<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion, when he giveth Sentence against Malefactors. So (saith this great Apostle) to whom God had committed a care over all the Christian Churches, he saw a necessity of reproving this Church that was at <ns0:hi>Corinth,</ns0:hi> for enduring the <ns0:hi>incestuous person</ns0:hi> in their Communion, and not casting him out; for their Er<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rors about the <ns0:hi>Resurrection,</ns0:hi> for their <ns0:hi>Divisions, Schisms,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Contentions,</ns0:hi> &c. but he professeth, that he did this with many tears; and those not shed in hypocrisie, but forced from the anguish and affliction of his heart; that he had nothing less in his design, than to put them to any excessive grief or trou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble, but what he wrote was out of a Principle of Love and good Will, both to the welfare of their whole Church, and to the good of the particular Souls of those that were the Mem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bers of that Church. Ministers or others do no good by their censures or reproofs, if they do not so dispense them, as peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple may see that what they do, or say, is out of their abun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dant love to their Souls.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 But if any hath caused grief, he hath not grie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ved me, but in part <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The Particle [<ns0:hi>if</ns0:hi>] doth not here signifie any <ns0:hi>doubting</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>uncertainty</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> (for the Incestuous person, of whom the Apostle here, and in the following verses, speaks, had certainly cau<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed grief both to the Apostle, and also to the Church whereof he was a Member.) It is as much as <ns0:hi>although</ns0:hi>; or the Apostle speaketh in this form, because by his repentance his grief was much allayed. But how doth the Apostle say, That he had grieved him <ns0:hi>but in part.</ns0:hi> Some think he saith so, because the Apostles grief for his sin, was now turned into joy by his repen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tance: Others think, that those words, <ns0:hi>in part,</ns0:hi> signifie that it was not the whole Church that had grieved him<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but only a part of it, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> this incestuous person, and those who took part with him. Others say, the Apostle saith, <ns0:hi>in part,</ns0:hi> to let us know, that it was not a grief to him only, but to them also. The last would bid very fair for the sense of the place; if the Apostle had not in his first Epistle, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 5.2. said, <ns0:hi>That they were puffed up,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>had not mourned.</ns0:hi> So as I judge the second more like to be the sense of the Apostle, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> That it was not the whole Church that had grieved him, but a part of it only: and therefore the next words are added.</ns0:note>: that I may not overcharge you all <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>That I may not over charge you all,</ns0:hi> that is, that I might not load you all with that imputation, as if you were all involved in it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 Sufficient to such a man <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> this <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>censure.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> punishment <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">This verse maketh it clear, that by <ns0:hi>any, v.</ns0:hi> 5. he meaneth the incestuous person, mentioned in the first Epistle, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 5. whom he had ordered to be cast out, and delivered to Satan; which (as appeareth from this verse) they had done<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> which is the <ns0:hi>punishment</ns0:hi> mentioned in this verse. They who think, that the punishment here mentioned was not <ns0:hi>Excommunication,</ns0:hi> but another <ns0:hi>being delivered to Satan, and vexed by him:</ns0:hi> 1. Beg a grave Question, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> Whether <ns0:hi>delivering to Satan in this place signifieth any more, than a casting of the person out of Christs King<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom on Earth (which is his Church) and making him one of the World again, of which Satan is the God?</ns0:hi> 2. They seem not to con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sider, <ns0:hi>That if this Church had delivered him to Satan, they could have done no more:</ns0:hi> So as the Apostle would not have said, <ns0:hi>Suffi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cient is this punishment,</ns0:hi> when it was the greatest that they could inflict. Some object, That it is not probable that the Apostle (had he been cast out of the Communion of the Church, for so notorious a crime) would have given order for his being re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stored in so short a time, as was that betwixt his writing the first, and this his second Epistle. 1. Some think, that he was as yet only under a suspension, and the Church had not pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceeded to Excommunication: this Opinion is favoured by the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> word here used, which is <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, the gentlest of all the words in use in that Language to express punishment by. 2. Though in the times following the Apostles, a longer time was set after Excommunication, for testifying the repentance of Sinners notoriously scandalous, before the Church did again ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mit them into her Fellowship; yet that it was so in the Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stles time, is more than appears. Possibly it might be so or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dered afterwards, when, as the Church multiplied, so sin more abounded; and they might from many experiences of relapses, be quickened to make such Orders. 3. The Gift of <ns0:hi>discerning Spirits</ns0:hi> was more usual in the Apostles times than afterward; so that though in following times, when the Apostles were dead, and the extraordinary Gift of discerning Spirits was fail<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed or abated, the Church being not able any other way to judge of the truth of Sinners repentance, than from their chan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ged life and conversation, which asked time, might set a long<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er time for such Penitents; yet there might not be the same reason for the Apostles doing it. 4. Notwithstanding any thing that appears, there might be the distance of a year or two be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />twixt <ns0:hi>Pauls</ns0:hi> writing these two <ns0:hi>Epistles.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, which <ns0:hi>was inflicted</ns0:hi> of many <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Who these <ns0:hi>many</ns0:hi> were, by whom the Apostle saith this <ns0:hi>punishment</ns0:hi> was inflicted, is a little disputed; whether the <ns0:hi>Presbytery,</ns0:hi> or the <ns0:hi>Community?</ns0:hi> Their Opinion seemeth (to me) best, who think that the Offi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cers of the Church of <ns0:hi>Corinth</ns0:hi> heard and judged of matters of Faith, and reported it to the Community; but he was not cast out without the consent and approbation of the Community.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:461" />7 So that contrariwise, <ns0:hi>ye ought</ns0:hi> rather to forgive <ns0:hi>him,</ns0:hi> and comfort <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Forgi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="4 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ss in this place doth not signifie the taking away, or <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> of the guilt of sin, (that i<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Gods work, not mans) but remitt<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>g of the <ns0:hi>punishment.</ns0:hi> And <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>his maketh that proba<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble, That they had not as yet proceeded with this person to Excommunication; only kept him (like a suspected Leper, without the Camp) out of a Communion with the Church: Or if they had actually cast him out, <ns0:hi>forgiving</ns0:hi> here can signifie nothing, but <ns0:hi>restoring him</ns0:hi> again to a full Communion with them; which is also the <ns0:hi>comforting</ns0:hi> which is here mentioned.</ns0:note>, lest perhaps such a one should be swallo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                     <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap> up with overmuch sorrow <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">It is plain from hence, That the Apostle had intelligence, that this person expressed abundant sorrow; otherwise he would not have expressed his fear of his being drowned in his own tears. Though the condition of such, at this day, is sad e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nough, who are regularly cast out of the Communion of any true Church of Christ, for crimes which deserve such a punish<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment; yet we must imagine it much sadder <ns0:hi>then.</ns0:hi> Now Chur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ches are multiplied, whole Cities and Nations are Christiani<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />zed; and though a person be cast out of a Church, yet it is not so taken notice of, but he may yet have converse with other Christians, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> but there, the greater part of the City being Heathens<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and the whole <ns0:hi>Countries</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Achaia</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Greece</ns0:hi> (con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tiguous to it) being Heathens; one cast out of the Communion of the Church, (if he had the least sense of Religion) could not but be deeply afflicted to be in such a case, as none but Heathens and professed Idolaters would keep him company, or have any intimacy with him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 Wherefore I beseech you, that ye would con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />firm <ns0:hi>your</ns0:hi> love towards him <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">That you would restore him to a Communion with you in your Church-Assemblies, and take him into the bosom of your Church again, and be (as before) friendly towards him. The word which we translate <ns0:hi>confirm,</ns0:hi> is <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, which sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifieth <ns0:hi>authoritatively</ns0:hi> to establish or confirm. Some observe, That the Apostle speaks to them as <ns0:hi>Iudges,</ns0:hi> to gain their good opinion, and make them more pliable, whereas he might authoritatively have absolved him. It is hard to say, what Authority the <ns0:hi>Apostles</ns0:hi> had or had not, to excommunicate; but we want a Precedent in holy Writ of the Apostles, or, any of them, exercising such a Power, as being absent; and so in no capacity to hear the proof of any Fact against scandalous persons. <ns0:hi>Paul,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 5. writes to the <ns0:hi>Church of Corinth</ns0:hi> to do it, and doth only himself command them to do their du<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty; and here again he writeth to them to forgive him, and restore him. There being no mention, either in the former Epistle, or here, of any Command that the <ns0:hi>incestuous person</ns0:hi> should put away his Wife taken unlawfully; or that he did any such thing in testification of his Repentance, makes it ve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry probable, that his crime was not using his Fathers Wife, as his Wife, but as his Harlot; had it been otherwise, we should, very probably, have read of something in the one or the other place, signifying such a Command of the Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stle, or the thing done by him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 For to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether ye be obedient in all things <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">As for other ends, so for this also I wrote my former Epi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stle to you, and I now write this second Epistle to you also, that I might have an experiment of you, what regard you would shew to that Apostolical Authority, wherewith God hath invested me.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 To whom ye forgive any thing, I <ns0:hi>forgive</ns0:hi> also: for if I forgave any thing, to whom I for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gave <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> for your sakes <ns0:hi>forgave I it,</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>in the sight.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> in the person of Christ <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">The word so often repeated in this verse, and translated <ns0:hi>forgive,</ns0:hi> is <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, which signifies to <ns0:hi>give,</ns0:hi> or gratifie, or do a kindness, as well as to <ns0:hi>forgive.</ns0:hi> So as it needeth not always to be interpreted of any judicial act of <ns0:hi>Absolution.</ns0:hi> If you see reason to remit any thing of the punishment inflicted upon the incestuous person, I am satisfied with what you do, I shall take no offence at you for it. If I have shewed any favour to any person amongst you that hath fallen under my reproof and chastisement, it hath been for your sake, for the good and advantage of your Church, or upon their motion and intercession; and I have done it sincerely in the sight of Christ (the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> is, in the <ns0:hi>face of Christ</ns0:hi>).</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 Lest Satan should get an advantage of us <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">As I have done it in kindness to you, so I have also done it for the advantage both of that person, who is so forgiven, and of your whole Church, which is concerned in the welfare, or miscarriage of every individual Member. <ns0:hi>Lest Satan should get advantage of us</ns0:hi>; The <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> is, <ns0:hi>That we be not overcome by Satan:</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> properly signifies to get again, or to gain a Superiority, to get the upper hand. The advantage Satan was like to get by their continuing severity to this offender, was either by his <ns0:hi>over-much Grief,</ns0:hi> or by the <ns0:hi>hardning of his Heart:</ns0:hi> So as he seeing no probability to be restored again to his Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />munion with the Church, should be exposed, either to tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ptations to some desperate courses, (which are often the ef<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fects of minds full of sorrow and discontent) or else to courses of Idolatry, or loosness, in giving up himself to the Devils Kingdom in the World, because he could not be admitted into the Church, which is the Kingdom of Christ.</ns0:note>: for we are not ignorant of his devices <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">For (saith the Apostle) <ns0:hi>We are not ignorant of his devices,</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, his thoughts and counsels, how he continually walketh about both like a <ns0:hi>roaring Lion, seeking whom he may devour</ns0:hi>; and like an old <ns0:hi>Serpent,</ns0:hi> seeking whom and how he may deceive. This lets us know, with how much <ns0:hi>Prudence,</ns0:hi> those who are trusted with the Souls of others, ought to manage their Reproofs, or severe dealings with others; the end of all these is the amend<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment and reformation of such persons, not their spiritual ruine and destruction: and all <ns0:hi>Reproofs</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Censures</ns0:hi> must be given, and made, and managed with reference to that end. We have not only the concern of Gods Glory (which is the main) to be looked at, but the good also of their Souls, whom we so re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />prove, censure, or alienate our selves from; and indeed, with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out consulting this, we cannot consult Gods Glory; who hath told us, That he <ns0:hi>desireth not the death of a sinner, but rather that he should turn from his wickedness, and live:</ns0:hi> and therefore we must have an <ns0:hi>Eye</ns0:hi> about us, and beneath us, to the Devil, as well as above us to God; and prudently judge how such affli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctive and harsh actions may be so done by us, that in the mean time <ns0:hi>Satan</ns0:hi> get no advantage, and we lose the Souls of those with whom we so deal, instead of gaining them to God; which is the main and principal End we ought in all those actions to aim at, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 4.5. so 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.20.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 Furthermore, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts 16.8.</ns0:note> when I came to Troas to <ns0:hi>preach</ns0:hi> Christs gospel, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 16.9<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note> a door was opened unto me of the Lord <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">This <ns0:hi>Troas</ns0:hi> was either the City, or the whole Country cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led <ns0:hi>Troy</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Ilium,</ns0:hi> or the lesser <ns0:hi>Phrygia.</ns0:hi> We read of <ns0:hi>Pauls</ns0:hi> go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing thither by Sea from <ns0:hi>Philippi, Acts</ns0:hi> 20.6, 7. and of his ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving been there, 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 4.13. He tells us, That the business why he went thither, was to preach the Gospel; for it was not the <ns0:hi>Apostles</ns0:hi> business to stay, as fixed Ministers, in any one place, but to carry the Gospel up and down the World to several pla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces; which they did by virtue of their general Commission to <ns0:hi>Go, preach, and baptize all Nations</ns0:hi>; though sometimes they had a more special Call and Commission, as <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> had, to go into <ns0:hi>Macedonia.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>door opened,</ns0:hi> either signifieth the free li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />berty he had there to preach, or the great success which God gave him in his work; which he elsewhere calleth an <ns0:hi>Effectual door.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 I had no rest in my spirit, because I found not Titus my brother; but taking my leave of them, I went from thence into Macedonia <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">He tells us, That when he came there, he was much trou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bled, because he did not find his <ns0:hi>Brother Titus,</ns0:hi> where the hu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mility of this great Apostle is considerable, in that he disdain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed not to call <ns0:hi>Titus</ns0:hi> (a person, though a Minister, yet much in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />feriour to him as an Apostle) <ns0:hi>Brother.</ns0:hi> Several reasons are gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven of <ns0:hi>Pauls</ns0:hi> trouble. That which is most probable, is, That he did expect at <ns0:hi>Troas</ns0:hi> to have met with <ns0:hi>Titus</ns0:hi> come from <ns0:hi>Co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rinth,</ns0:hi> from whom he might more perfectly have understood the affairs of that Church: not finding him there, he tells us he went forward into <ns0:hi>Macedonia</ns0:hi>; whither, after the uproar at <ns0:hi>Ephesus,</ns0:hi> he designed to go, (as we read <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 20.1.) but went first into <ns0:hi>Greece,</ns0:hi> and stayed there three months, intending to come to <ns0:hi>Macedonia</ns0:hi> in his return, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 Now thanks <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">The Translation of the Greek here, is not certain: For to translate it word for word, it is, <ns0:hi>But thanks be to God al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ways, triumphing us in Christ:</ns0:hi> which makes it uncertain, whe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther there be not a defect of a Preposition; upon the supply of which, it would be, <ns0:hi>Who triumpheth over us in Christ</ns0:hi>; having subdued our hearts to the Kingdom and Obedience of Christ. But the most Interpreters rather agree with our Translators, and think the sense of the Apostle is, <ns0:hi>Who maketh us to triumph.</ns0:hi> In the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> there is a Conjugation, where the <ns0:hi>Active Verb</ns0:hi> signifieth <ns0:hi>to make another to do a thing</ns0:hi>; and there are several instances brought by Learned men out of the <ns0:hi>Septuagi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>,</ns0:hi> where the <ns0:hi>Active Verb</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> also hath that sense; that which cometh nearest it in the <ns0:hi>Original</ns0:hi> in holy Writ, is, That, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.26. where the Spirit is said <ns0:hi>to make intercession for us,</ns0:hi> be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause it causeth us to make intercession. According to this, the sense is, Blessed be God, who, though we meet with many Enemies, yet through Christ he maketh us more than Conque<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rours, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.37. so that we are not overcome by any of them, but on the contrary, we triumph over them as conque<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red by us</ns0:note>, and maketh ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">And this by manifesting by us in every place the <ns0:hi>savour of the Knowledge of Christ</ns0:hi>; that is, of the Gospel. He calleth it a <ns0:hi>Savour,</ns0:hi> either with allusion to that sweet per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fumed Oyntment, with which the High-Priest, under the Law, was anointed, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 30.23. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 133.2. or with reference to the Incense used also under the Law; or with relation to <ns0:hi>Solomons</ns0:hi> expression, <ns0:hi>Cant.</ns0:hi> 1.3. where we read of the <ns0:hi>Savour of Christs good Oyntments,</ns0:hi> and that his Name is as an <ns0:hi>Oyntment poured forth.</ns0:hi> By the <ns0:hi>Savour</ns0:hi> of the Knowledge of Christ here mentioned, the Apostle plainly meaneth the <ns0:hi>Reputation</ns0:hi> or good report that the Gospel had in every place: s<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e <ns0:hi>Hos.</ns0:hi> 14.7.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:461" />15 For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 1.18.</ns0:note> in them that are saved, and in them that perish <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">For the God whom we serve, doth not judge of us, nor will reward us according to our success, but according to our faithfulness and diligence in his work. We give unto all a good savour by our Doctrine; and our labours are a sweet sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vour in the nostrils of God, whatever effects they have upon Souls. God accepteth of our labours as to good men, to whom we are Instruments of Eternal Life and Salvation; and though others despise the Gospel, and refuse the sweet sound of it, yet as to them also we are a sweet savour in the nostrils of God: Though <ns0:hi>Israel be not saved</ns0:hi> (saith the Prophet) <ns0:hi>yet I shall be glorified.</ns0:hi> It is not for any neglect in us, as to our du<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty, if any perish, but from their own wilfulness and perversness.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 2.34.</ns0:note> To the one <ns0:hi>we are</ns0:hi> the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life <ns0:hi>w</ns0:hi>: And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">C<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>p. 3.5, 6.</ns0:note> who is sufficient for these things? <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">As sweet Smells, which are to some pleasant and com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fortable, are to others pernicious and deadly; so it is with the sweet savour of the Gospel. The Report which we in all places make of Christ, to some, through their unbelief and hardness of heart, and fondness of their lusts, proveth but the favour of <ns0:hi>death unto death</ns0:hi>; hardening their hearts to their Eternal ruine and destruction: but to such, who being ordain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed to Eternal Life, believe our reports, and embrace the Go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />spel, and live up to the Precepts and Rule of it, our preach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing proves a cause of spiritual and of <ns0:hi>Eternal Life,</ns0:hi> to which that leadeth.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">And O how great a work is this? What man? What Angel is sufficient for it? It is a mighty work to preach the Gospel as we ought to preach it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 For we are not as many, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">C<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 4.2.</ns0:note> which <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> corrupt the word of God; but as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God, speak we <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> in Christ <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Lest the false Apostles and Teachers in this Church should <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>light this Exclamation of the Apostles, and the pretended difficulty he made of the Ministerial work; the Apostle adds these words, I confess (saith he) it is no very difficult thing to speak of Christ, and pretend to preach and do as much as I do; but there are many <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, we translate it, <ns0:hi>corrupt</ns0:hi> the Word; the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> word signifies, <ns0:hi>To sell wine or vi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctuals for money,</ns0:hi> and because such kind of people make no con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />science to deceive, cheat, and deal fraudulently with their Cu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stomers: it is sometimes used to signifie <ns0:hi>corrupting</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>deceiving.</ns0:hi> We are not (saith the Apostle) of the number of those who in preaching meerly serve their own bellies; and turn the Church into a Tavern or Victualling-house, making a gain of the Gospel, and discoursing a little while in a Pulpit for gain; and so making no conscience, either what they speak, or how they speak. But we speak by Authority from Christ, and in Christs Name; cloathed with his Authority, and as his Ambassa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dors; and so dare not say any thing unto people, and deliver to his people what he never gave us any Commission to speak; nor yet to speak whatever cometh at our tongues end, but we must remember, that we are in the sight of God, and speak as from God of God; and that not fraudulently, but sincerely; sincerely aiming at the Glory of God in what we do, and the Salvation of the Souls of them to whom we speak. This is a great work, first to consult the Mind and Will of God, and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> it out by study and meditation; then faithfully to com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />municate it unto people, without any vain or corrupt mixtures (which do but adulterate the Word preached) then to apply it to the Consciences of those that hear us. <ns0:hi>Who is sufficient for these things?</ns0:hi> that is, to discharge the Office of the Ministry in the preaching of the Gospel, as men ought to preach it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
